header.interval_method: score (Wilson) for single proportions; score interval for paired differences
header.forbidden_inference: These intervals are MARGINAL, not simultaneous. No claim of the form 'X exceeds Y' may be derived from two intervals failing to overlap: non-overlap is neither necessary nor sufficient for a difference, and several rows in this table are not independent of each other. Where a difference is claimed, use the paired_difference field on the dependent row.

why_this_file_exists: Three competitors across roughly seven datasets and several vocabularies is plausibly a few
dozen paired tests. Under the null, several of those clear the conventional threshold by
chance alone. Choosing the family or the correction after seeing the output is p-hacking, so
the declaration is committed BEFORE any comparison run is fired and is consumed by the
reporting code rather than applied by hand.

families.description: BioMapper against each incumbent identifier-mapping service, run on identical rows with the identical scorer.
families.unit_of_analysis: one input row, keyed by the dataset's row id
families.pairing: genuine: the same rows are scored by every arm, so McNemar applies
families.correction_rationale: The primary family controls the family-wise error rate: a single false claim that BioMapper beats a named incumbent is the costly error here, so the stricter control is the right one.
families.primary_comparison: BioMapper versus the best-performing incumbent on the CURIE-backbone dataset, strict correctness flag
families.gate_note: Requires live calls to three external hosted services. Declared here; fired separately as a supervised step.

families.description: Within one dataset, the strict correctness flag against a relaxed variant of the same flag (charge-normalized, equivalence-set) over the same rows.
families.pairing: genuine and nested: the relaxed flag is a superset of the strict flag on the same rows, so the contrast is paired by construction and the two marginal intervals are NOT independent
families.correction_rationale: Descriptive contrasts characterising where relaxation helps, not claims of superiority over a competitor. Controlling the false-discovery rate keeps power where a family-wise correction would spend it for no decision benefit.
families.primary_comparison: strict versus equivalence-set on the reference metabolite set
families.gate_note: Computed offline from an already-committed suite directory; no calls.

rules: Every reported p-value names its family. A p-value with no declared family is a protocol violation, not a finding.
The correction is applied within family, over every test in the family that was RUN, not only those that were reported.
Marginal intervals are not simultaneous. No claim of the form 'X exceeds Y' may be derived from two intervals failing to overlap.
Where pairing does not genuinely exist, no difference statistic is emitted and the absence is recorded with its reason.
